fp1Pan.reading: no shimmer or shadow crawl to see at 4141 m from the origin: frame k at the far place differs from frame k at the engine origin by less than two moved worlds differ from each other. What can be measured: the pan is less even at the far place (frame to frame change 0.0406 to 0.0961 against 0.0412 to 0.0504 near the origin), because a 2 mm camera step lands on a 0.24 mm grid there. That is under a pixel at this step size
fp1Pan.note: frameToFrame: mean absolute difference (0 to 255) between one pan frame and the next, per mode. farAgainstNear: frame k at the far place against frame k with the world moved to the engine origin; nearAgainstNear2 is the same comparison between two moved worlds, both near the origin. changedShare is the share of pixels that differ by more than 16 of 255. The worst far against near pair is saved eight times stronger as a picture.

howMeasured: The stitch code (tools/bake/stitch/, TypeScript, run by node harness/bench/stitch.mjs) bakes the whole stitched world twice in one Node process; bake.ms is the second run. Counts are read from the finished data: ports from the roads cut at the clip line, closures one per port, connector grades and clearances from the lane model that built them, landmark positions from the T1 tile bytes. The Godot run loads the 250 m tiles (each placed by its origin only), takes one shot per pose, reads the landmark pins and node transforms back from the engine, and runs a slow pan of 24 frames at the far district three times: as baked, and twice with the whole world moved so that the place sits near the engine origin.

data.ground: GEDTM30 v1.2 smoothed over 60 m (the P0-018 pick) inside a district; outside, the districts' grounds blended by 1 / distance squared to each clip line; one 12.5 m lattice

checks.openBoundaryPortsNote: ports with no closure at all (a road that would end in the air). Big ports with no connector yet are closed by a barrier and listed under portsWaitingForAConnector.
checks.landmarkNote: expected: district offset plus the projection of the OSM node (degrees) around the district origin. baked: the pin of that node read back from the T1 tile bytes (32-bit floats relative to the tile, plus the tile origin). The pin was placed from the projected map model, so the error covers the origin, the offset, the tile cut and the float format.

relativeLayout.note: real: geodesic distance and bearing on the WGS84 ellipsoid (Vincenty), which shares no code with the projection. baked: between the mean pin positions read from the tiles.

rotation.tilesCarry: an origin only: a T1 tile has no rotation or scale field
rotation.note: per district: the Jacobian of district metres to world metres against the identity, the angle between true north at the frame origin and -Z, and the sign of east x north. The Godot scene adds its own count of nodes whose basis is not the identity.

fp1.float32StepNote: a 32-bit float steps by 0.244 mm between 2,048 and 4,096 m and by 0.488 mm between 4,096 and 8,192 m, per axis
fp1.note: vertices are stored relative to their 250 m tile, so their own rounding is 0.015 to 0.03 mm; what is left is the tile origin and the camera, which are world positions in 32-bit floats. The pan numbers are in the Godot part of the report.

bake.note: ms is the second of two runs in one Node process (the first includes code warm-up). It covers frames, clip, ports, the ground lattice, the three connectors through the lane model, closures, content, the T1 encode and the checks. sourceLoadMs is reading the pilot downloads and smoothing the height data, before the bake. The times double when another program keeps the machine busy (hostLoadPerCore over 1): a calm run is about 2.4 s.

productionNeeds: One road graph for a district and its connectors. Here a district road is a plain ribbon that stops at the clip line and the connector is a separate lane model site, so the join is two meshes that meet (with an apron where the clip line is oblique). Production cuts the district graph at the port node and gives that node to the connector, so lanes, kerbs and heights run through.

Clip lines that cross a big road at a right angle, at a place with no slip road. Where the line is oblique the two carriageways of one street become two ports (Vikas Marg at Laxmi Nagar: 27 m apart along the road).
A connector for every big port, or a rule that turns the port into a district-internal end. The list is in filler.needAnAuthoredConnector.

The edge band and the generated back streets want the same strip of land. Here a shell is dropped where a generated street or a connector runs; production should run the back street behind the first row of shells, or pick per port.
Filler ground with a height rule of its own (river banks, embankments) and filler blocks from area profiles along connectors: the bench has ground and water only.
A constrained ground under connectors (TF2 from the road bench) in place of the lattice that is pressed to the connector height.
Rail, river and metro as their own connector kinds: the thing under the flyover is a two lane road standing in for the railway.
Clip polygons and connectors drawn and reviewed in the map inspector; the waypoint table lives in a script today.
Height offsets solved over all districts and ports together (least squares over the port height steps), not one median per district.
The download box of a district 100 m larger than its clip on every side, so the edge band is complete (clip.dc3.perDistrict.lineWithDataOutside).
